a hosted schedule runs or succeeds; confirm hosted state before a cutover.

Scheduled Vercel opportunities total 2,887 per day in this repository. Moving
only the schedule does not reduce processor invocations; processor moves do.

## Overlap safety classes

Cutover safety depends on whether two owners can run the same slot without
duplicating a side effect. Cron Control's slot claim deduplicates its own ticks,
not a concurrent Vercel tick.

| Class | Meaning | Cutover order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim-fenced | The processor atomically claims rows, leases or batches | Enable Cloudflare, verify one cycle, then remove the Vercel entry |
| Idempotent | Repeat runs converge (upsert, overwrite, delete-if-unreferenced) | Same as claim-fenced; overlap only costs a duplicate run |
| Handover | A concurrent run can duplicate a notification or email | Remove the old owner first, confirm its last run, then enable Cloudflare |

## pg_cron jobs

Live jobs after replaying every migration's schedule and unschedule calls.
`process-notification-batches` was unscheduled by a later migration.

| Job | Cadence | Work | Decision and justification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fetch-exchange-rates` | `0 6 * * *` | `pg_net` POST to Web `/api/cron/finance/exchange-rates` | Move to Cron Control (`finance-exchange-rates`): Postgres is acting as an HTTP scheduler |
| `update_expired_sessions_job` | every minute | One UPDATE closing expired Nova sessions | Retain: pure SQL in the database |
| typing-indicator cleanup (unnamed) | every minute | DELETE stale typing indicators | Retain: pure SQL in the database |
| `security-budget-cleanup` | every minute | DELETE at most 20,000 expired budget counters | Retain: pure SQL, already bounded |
| `refresh-posts-dashboard` | `*/10 * * * *` | REFRESH one materialized view | Retain: pure SQL in the database |
| `cleanup-rate-limits` | `*/15 * * * *` | DELETE expired rate-limit windows | Retain: pure SQL in the database |
| `normalize-task-sort-keys` | `0 * * * *` | Renumber task sort keys | Retain: pure SQL in the database |
| `hard-delete-soft-deleted-items` | `5 * * * *` | DELETE tasks and boards soft-deleted over 30 days ago | Retain: pure SQL; storage objects belong to `tasks-cleanup-media` |

**Retained exceptions.** Each retained job runs a single statement against
Postgres tables with no HTTP, storage or provider side effect. A Cloudflare
trigger would add a Worker invocation and a service-key HTTP round trip per tick
to execute the same SQL in the same database: more cost and credential exposure,
no compute moved off Supabase. Owners should still review the three every-minute
jobs' cadence. Any job that gains an outbound call loses its exception.

## Next.js `after()` continuations

These run after the response on the hosting function, with no durable owner. A
crashed or recycled function silently loses them.

| Site | Work | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Infrastructure Zalo personal channel route | Phone contact sync job | Queue consumer with persisted job state |
| Infrastructure and inventory-core Polar product sync helpers | Product catalog sync after webhooks | Queue consumer |
| Inventory Square webhook route | Catalog sync from Square | Queue consumer |
| Teach AI feedback route | AI feedback generation | Queue consumer |
| Web notes voice-jobs route | Voice transcription job (reservation exists) | Queue consumer |
| Web AI-agent webhook route | Adapter `waitUntil` delivery | Queue consumer |
| Web accept-invite and decline-invite routes | Invitation notification finalization | `ctx.waitUntil` (bounded, best effort) once Worker-hosted |

## Processors without a hosted schedule

These routes exist but no Vercel entry, pg_cron job or Worker trigger calls
them. They may have relied on the retired Docker runner; confirm the intended
owner before scheduling any of them.

| Route | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Pay `payment/orders`, `payment/subscriptions` | Cron Control job if reconciliation is required |
| Inventory `inventory/polar-product-sync` | Cron Control job if webhook sync is insufficient |
| Tasks `tasks/generate-embeddings` | Queue consumer for embedding backlog |
| Web `ai/sync-models`, `discord/daily-report`, `discord/wol/daily/remind` | Cron Control job when an owner confirms the need |
| Hive `hive/simulate` | Retire: the catalog keeps it disabled |

Workspace managed cron jobs (`workspace_cron_jobs`) have a due-job claim RPC
but no live scheduler since the Docker runner retired; only run-now routes
execute them. A Cron Control job draining that claim RPC is the target, gated on
a product decision because enabling it starts user-defined outbound requests.

## Existing Cloudflare owner

`apps/cron-control` runs every five minutes, requeues stale push batches and
calls the Web immediate-delivery processor only when a pending immediate batch
exists. See [Cloudflare Cron Control](/build/devops/cloudflare-cron-control).

## Phase 1: `pay-products` scheduler qualification

`pay-products` is the first scheduler move because it runs twice per day and the
existing processor converges product rows with provider-ID upserts. Cron Control
already declares the same `0 */12 * * *` schedule and the authenticated Pay
processor route. The dispatch regression now pins its per-slot request bound,
single transient retry, duplicate-slot behavior, and durable stop after five
failed slots across ledger reconstruction.

This phase qualifies source behavior only. `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` remains
empty in `apps/cron-control/cloudflare.config.ts`, and the Vercel declaration
remains active in `apps/pay/vercel.json`. Do not change either until an authorized
production rollout has installed the Pay origin and matching cron secret, shown
one successful Cloudflare slot, and recorded the Vercel last-run boundary. The
old Vercel schedule stays the owner until then. Roll back a later cutover by
stopping/removing `pay-products` from Cron Control and restoring its Vercel entry.

The five scheduled GitHub workflows are operational automation rather than
product background work: `.github/workflows/mobile-testflight-review-queue.yaml`
drains a release-review queue; `release-please-auto-merge.yaml` handles release
branches; `actions-storage-report.yaml` reports CI artifact storage;
`security-checks.yaml` runs security scans; and
`security-review-sweep.yaml` handles security-review automation. They remain on
GitHub Actions and are not part of the product scheduler migration.

## Migration waves

1. **Scheduler cutover.** Qualify and then move `pay-products` first, preserving
   its 12-hour cadence, default-off behavior, auth contract and per-slot
   operation envelope. Continue with `tasks-cleanup-media`, trust-cache,
   calendar-provider sync, and the claim-fenced Web jobs. Move handover jobs only
   after their old owner is removed and its last run is confirmed. Move the
   exchange-rate `pg_net` call to Cron Control; keep the seven pure-SQL jobs in
   Postgres under the existing exception.
2. **Worker processors.** Keep checkout expiry as the tested template, then
   move cleanup media with a durable cursor, product sync with bounded
   pagination/upserts, and trust-cache writes with their 32-write concurrency
   cap. Keep the `pay-products` Worker processor default-off until the Worker
   path has exact-artifact and runtime acceptance.
3. **Queues and workflows.** Move notification, email, announcement and report
   delivery, calendar provider sync, then the `after()` sites, with retry budgets
   aligned to their existing claims and persisted progress.
4. **Retirements.** Confirm with Infrastructure owners whether to retire the
   Docker-era sampler and alerts; retire the disabled Hive simulation route only
   after its owner confirms there is no remaining need.

Per-job cutover steps live in the
[Cron Control runbook](/build/devops/cloudflare-cron-control); processor targets
and cost bounds live in [processor migration](/build/devops/cloudflare-processor-migration).
